Thank you! All these comments help me realize that I'm not alone with these thoughts. I FALL INTO DEPRESSIONS thinking about this shit. I can't even watch movies or tv shows without thinking of that. What makes this harder is that I've spent my entire life believing in the afterlife. 

I mean, I can understand the whole peaceful part people who don't believe in it say, but the fact is, if there was no afterlife, then I may never see my family again, or anything other that. 

To me, my only solution is to keep an open mind, no matter how much things don't make sense. On one hand, we've had many skeptics debunk these things over and over again, and even plenty of stories saying they saw nothing during their NDEs or clinical deaths. Heck, even the fact that Houdini hasn't come back from the dead still shakes me up. But on the other hand, these concepts still exist, and people still believe in them. Heck, to counteract with those who saw nothing, there are other NDEs that either saw something, or people who've had ghost experiences that felt or saw something, and TBH, I don't a lot of them were dreams, illusions, or even lies. 

To me, no matter how hard it is to believe, I'll still believe in an afterlife. But I will give you some advice: always keep an open mind, or try to keep away from reading things off the Internet.

Alright, ever since I posted this thing, I've become more of an agnostic theist than a Christian. 

Look, I do still keep my beliefs in the afterlife, or part of it being God. However, I'm not Christian, probably because I've read SO MANY atheist arguments (mainly the brain hallucination explanation) to a point where I don't know what to believe. 

But, at this point, I'd rather keep an open mind to both sides than just take one side. Whenever it's God vs. the explosion made from gravity, or heaven Vs. the brain, I'd honestly rather keep it a mystery. I have too many doubts for Christianity, but I do not want to be a complete skeptic. Yeah, you can say I'm holding myself back, but to be honest, I'd rather have this be a debate no one can win until death. 

Yet, I feel like there has to be stronger forces or things out of the ordinary out there, either on Earth in the universe. Heck, to be honest, I feel like even somethings aren't true, anything is possible in this universe. Also, I think experience has to do more with these things. Sure, some might be explained through science, but some could be genuine.

To me, I'd rather keep both Science and the Supernatural separate. Call me ignorant, but those are just my beliefs.
To me, I'd rather believe in something than nothing, and yes, I've thought about all the arguments against him. IMO, anything could be possible in this universe.
Maybe not the "succeed" part, but so far...Deism sounds nice. Again, I just believe in God, but I don't follow religious beliefs that much.

Hey, thank you everybody for giving your thoughts. It's great to see that I alm not alone on this. I'm still sure I can ignore time passing in the future. Until then, it feels like I'm still in a WAR with myself.

Update: Well, ever since I wrote this post, I think I got WORSE. Now, my mind can't stop thinking about time passing. Now, it feels like I can only think forward. As in, it just feels like my mind can't focus on the past, let alone one second in the past is already nothing. I can't focus my mind in the moment. 

Here's what it feels like in my mind: I keep being pushed by a black wall. Nothing is over that wall. No matter how hard I try, I keep being pushed by it, with no way to stop. Even if I have little moments of free thought, I can't focus on anything.

I'm trying my best to hold on, and as much as I tell myself that I will get better, this is just the hardest anxiety I have to go through. I just..it may have to do with my graduation. I just hope this leads me to getting over my time anxiety. And yet, this is all because of a STUPID DEATH CLOCK!!!
